intro.title: Generic List<T>
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Angular component that displays a list of items of any type, such as a list of users, products, or tasks. You will learn how to use TypeScript generics, specifically the `List<T>` pattern, to create flexible and type-safe components. The main technologies involved are Angular components and TypeScript's generic type parameters. By the end, you'll understand how to write components that work with different data types while maintaining full type checking and IntelliSense support.
intro.usecase: Generic List<T> is a foundational pattern for building reusable, type-safe data components in Angular applications. You'll use it to create dynamic data tables in admin dashboards, where each column can display different data types like strings, numbers, or dates while maintaining strict type checking. It's also essential for building filterable product catalogs in e-commerce sites, where the same list component can render products, categories, or user reviews without code duplication. This approach ensures your UI components are flexible, maintainable, and scalable across different data models.
